questions.prompt: Why does the host run a plugin's disposers in reverse order?
options: Because arrays are faster to read backwards
Because later setup steps often depend on earlier ones, so they must be undone first
Because the first disposer always throws
Because effects are registered in random order
questions.explanation: Undoing the last thing first means nothing is torn down while something set up after it still relies on it.

questions.prompt: A plugin mounts a child plugin with ctx.plugin. What happens to the child when the parent unloads?
options: It keeps running until the program exits
It must be unloaded by hand first, or the parent throws
It unloads too, because mounting it was an effect on the parent
It is moved to the root context
questions.explanation: plugin() is built on effect(), so the child's dispose is one of the parent's disposers and runs when the parent unloads.

questions.prompt: A plugin starts an interval but returns no disposer for it. The plugin is reloaded three times. How many intervals are running afterwards?
questions.explanation: The first load plus three reloads each start an interval, and none are ever cleared, so four run at once. This leak is why every registration needs a disposer.
